events.continuity_hook: This closes the Madison graduation plan after the flights, rental car, and west-side hotel were selected.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final Madison logistics pass for ceremony timing, Sunday brunch, airport and rental-car timing, seats, hotel room request, parking, and packing.
events.scenario_brief: One week before the Madison graduation weekend, Erin and her spouse have the Friday afternoon one-stop into Madison, the Sunday late-afternoon return, a compact rental car, and the west-side suite hotel booked. The family has added a 10:30 a.m. Sunday brunch near campus, which still fits the return if they leave downtown by noon, while Saturday ceremony parking now looks tighter than expected. The hotel has confirmed parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness access, but Erin still needs the room-location request, both travelers' seat selections, rental counter hours, and a compact graduation-and-weekend packing plan.

events.continuity_hook: This starts the next client-training episode after the family graduation weekend is off her calendar.
events.interaction_goal: Create a ranked first plan for arrival city, flight timing, rental car, one-hotel versus split-stay lodging, demo-case handling, and the clinic confirmations Erin should get before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After Madison, Erin is assigned a mid-June Central Texas clinic training loop with a Monday afternoon equipment handoff in Round Rock, Tuesday training in north Austin, a Wednesday clinic session near New Braunfels, and a Thursday debrief likely in San Antonio. She will have the rolling demo case again, so rental-car access and hotel parking matter more than a rideshare-only plan. A Sunday afternoon nonstop into Austin creates a calmer start, a Monday morning one-stop is cheaper but fragile, and flying into San Antonio first would add backtracking. Hotel choices include a north Austin suite property with strong reviews, pool, and fitness access but no hot tub, a downtown Austin hotel with better dining but expensive parking, and a possible San Antonio final-night hotel if she splits the stay.

events.continuity_hook: This follows the first Central Texas planning pass once the clinic times and city order become firm enough for booking.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the outbound and return flights, settle the split-stay hotel plan, set rental-car pickup and drop-off windows, and list the room, parking, seat, and expense steps for booking.
events.scenario_brief: The Central Texas network confirms the Monday Round Rock handoff at 2:00 p.m., the Tuesday north Austin session at 8:00 a.m., the Wednesday New Braunfels session at midday, and a Thursday 1:00 p.m. San Antonio wrap. That makes the Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Austin nonstop the safest outbound despite the extra hotel night. The lodging choice has narrowed to the north Austin suite hotel for the first two nights and a San Antonio medical-center hotel for the final night, both with strong enough reviews and parking; the San Antonio option has the better recovery amenities. Erin still needs to choose between a tighter Thursday evening return from San Antonio and a calmer Friday morning flight that adds one more hotel night.

events.continuity_hook: This is a narrow post-booking schedule change within the Central Texas clinic loop.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to move to the late Thursday connection or add the Friday morning nonstop, then outline the flight, hotel, rental-car, and clinic-notification steps for the chosen plan.
events.scenario_brief: After Erin books the Sunday nonstop to Austin, the split hotels, the rental car, and a Thursday evening San Antonio return, the New Braunfels clinic moves its hands-on portion to Thursday late afternoon. The booked return is now too tight once the drive, demo-case repack, fuel stop, rental return, and security are included. A late Thursday one-stop is available but has an awkward layover, while a Friday morning nonstop from San Antonio would be easier and only requires extending the hotel and rental car by one night.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Central Texas change after the Thursday schedule move pushed Erin to a Friday return.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final logistics pass for weather timing, toll roads, demo-case packing, hotel arrivals, rental return, airport cushion, seat selection, and the compact work-bag setup.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before the Central Texas departure, Erin has switched to the Friday morning nonstop from San Antonio, extended the final hotel night, and kept the rental car through the revised airport drop-off. Heat, scattered storms, and road work around north Austin could slow the first two clinic days, and the rolling demo case is again close to the checked-bag weight limit. The outbound window seat is set, but the return seat map has changed; the north Austin hotel confirms pool and fitness access but no hot tub, while the San Antonio hotel confirms all three recovery amenities.

events.continuity_hook: This begins the next conference-style trip after the June client-training loop wraps up.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked first plan for flight timing, airport choice, hotel area, event-block deadline, local transportation, return timing, and whether to plan around a possible spouse weekend extension.
events.scenario_brief: After the Central Texas week closes, Erin is asked to staff a late-July veterinary operations expo in Chicago. The expo sessions run Monday through Wednesday near the convention center, with an optional Sunday afternoon booth setup and a Thursday client breakfast still pending. A Sunday afternoon nonstop from Denver into O'Hare gives her time for setup, a Monday morning nonstop saves a hotel night but leaves little cushion, and Midway itineraries are cheaper but less convenient for the return options. Hotel choices include the event block closest to the meeting space with a high rate and limited wellness amenities, a better-reviewed South Loop hotel with pool and fitness access but no listed hot tub, and a River North property that would be better if her spouse joins for a weekend extension but adds commute time.
